podcast.body: This record was released as a package alongside a book of poetry with the same name. This two-for-one deal made the book one of the best-selling poetry books by a Canadian, selling 10,000 copies in the first 36 hours. When the book and album were later separated, the book sold another 10,000 copies on its own. "It sold 10,000 copies in the first 36 hours."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was Gord Downie's debut solo album, released in 2001. It was described as "pretty quirky stuff" compared to The Tragically Hip's music, featured "The Goddamn Band" (which included members from Dinny Resruund, Eric's Trip, and The Skyteegers), and was compared to the work of Tom Waits due to its spoken word elements, low-fi recording, and difficult-to-categorize music. The album reached number 26 on the Canadian charts. "Koch Machine Glow has been compared to the work of Tom Waits. Lots of spoken word. Lots of low-fi recording and music that's really really hard to categorize in Pigeon Hole."
